createdItems.title: Keep layer settings reachable when the layer toggle is off
createdItems.implementationBrief: For Fixations, Saccades, Heatmap, and Raw gaze, the settings button/chevron should remain clickable while the layer is toggled off. Opening it should show the settings, but the actual setting controls should be visibly disabled until the layer is enabled again.
request: I should be able to press the settings button for **Fixations**, **Saccades**,
**Heatmap**, and **Raw gaze** even when that layer's toggle is off. The
settings panel should open normally, while its actual setting controls are
greyed out until the layer is switched on.
background: This is the Scanpath rail's shared `toggle → ⚙️ style → 🧹 filter` layer
pattern in [controls.py](scanpath_studio/controls.py). The off state now
disables only the controls that change the hidden layer, not the affordance
used to inspect or prepare them — so a layer's styling can be set up before
**Disabling never rewrites a value.** Same contract `_mode_gate` already
keeps: a disabled Streamlit widget owns and keeps its key, and these are
`global_*` keys — share-link and saved-config wire format — so a layer toggle
must not clobber a deep-linked or restored setting. Pinned by a test.
The reason rides each control's own `help` (via `_gated_help`, so a gate
reason and a layer reason compose) rather than replacing it, which is what
keeps the row's tooltip useful in both states.
No new surface: this changes when an existing control is interactive, not
what it sets, so the deep link, CLI and headless API are untouched.
Related: #UX-80 (the one-line section rows), #UX-86 (Heatmap and Raw gaze as
the other reason a rail control greys).
decisions: Review the four layers with their toggles off: the ▾ opens onto the real controls, greyed, with a caption saying to turn the layer on. Two calls worth disagreeing with — the 🧹 Filter halves were included (they had the same empty popover, and the ask named the `toggle → ⚙️ style → 🧹 filter` pattern), and 📄 Stimulus was **not**, because it holds three independent layers with no single switch, so there is no one thing being off.
whatWasDone: Each layer section on the rail was gated `if show_<layer>:` around the whole
popover body, so switching a layer off left its ▾ clickable and **empty** —
the affordance said there was something there and the popover said otherwise.
The bodies now always render and grey instead. `controls._layer_off(label, off=)`
is a context manager that pushes a reason onto a small stack;
`controls._layer_gate` folds that reason into every control rendered inside,
and the three shared rail primitives consult it — `_labeled` (which is what
`_popover_selectbox` and nearly every row go through), `_numeric_slider` and
`_range_slider`, so the UX-9 typed box greys with its slider. One caption at
the head of the popover says why, for the user who never hovers a control.
Applied to all four layers named in the ask — 👁️ Fixations, ↗️ Saccades,
🔥 Heatmap, 🔵 Raw gaze — and to the two halves of the 🧹 Filter section that
belong to Fixations and Saccades, which had the same empty-popover shape for
Fixations keeps its existing exception: in **Animate** the toggle reads off
but is inert (the replay *is* the fixation trail), and the styling below is
still live — so that case greys nothing.
`tests/test_layer_settings_when_off.py` — 9 tests over the mechanism and over
the real rail, checking each layer's control both ways round.
